works.section: The Battle of Tours — by Edward Gibbon
works.title: The Invasion of Gaul
works.source: Edward Gibbon, The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, Vol. V, ch. LII · Project Gutenberg #735 · public domain
works.note: The “lazy” Merovingian kings, the rise of the mayors of the palace, and the Saracen tide sweeping up from Spain — ending on Gibbon’s famous vision of a Muslim Europe, where “the Koran would now be taught in the schools of Oxford.”

works.section: The Battle of Tours — by Edward Gibbon
works.title: The Battle of Tours
works.source: Edward Gibbon, The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, Vol. V, ch. LII · Project Gutenberg #735 · public domain
works.note: Christendom delivered “by the genius and fortune of one man.” Charles lets the invaders gorge on plunder, then breaks them at Tours — earning the surname Martel, the Hammer.

works.section: The Battle of Tours — by Edward Gibbon
works.title: The Saviour Condemned
works.source: Edward Gibbon, The History of the Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, Vol. V, ch. LII · Project Gutenberg #735 · public domain
works.note: The bitter irony: having spent church wealth to fund the defence, the saviour of Christendom was repaid by a synod declaring him damned — his soul “burning, to all eternity, in the abyss of hell.”
